1.1 EXTERIOR – ROOF COVERING
A. Roofing Material: Asphalt architectural shingles (approx. 20 sq). Estimated age: 7 years.
B. Slope/Pitch: 6/12 main slope; 8/12 on front dormer.
C. Decking: Plywood, 1/2" (assumed; no exposed decking observed).
D. Underlayment: Not visible; no lifting or exposure noted at time of inspection.

Findings:
- Numerous hail strikes observed on the south-facing slope and the west-facing slope. Strikes appear as dark, bruise-like marks on the shingle surface. Several shingles have lost granules, exposing fiberglass mat in localized areas.
- A cluster of strikes concentrated around the valley on the south side, near the chimney. Suspect impact zone.
- No obvious punctures or tears through the shingle mat were observed.
- The north-facing slope (rear of home) showed only scattered, light granule loss. No discernible hail strike pattern.
- Ridge cap shingles: 3 units show cracking and granule loss. Could be age-related; however, the cracking pattern is consistent with impact.
- Dormer flashing on the front elevation appears intact. No lifting or separation.
- One plumbing vent boot (rear slope) has a cracked rubber collar. The crack is a vertical split approx. 1.5" long. This may be age-related; however, the location on the hail-exposed slope is noted.

Roof Condition Summary: Hail damage observed on south and west slopes. North slope not impacted. Recommend replacement of the south and west slopes; north slope appears serviceable. This is a partial roof replacement scenario.

1.2 EXTERIOR – GUTTERS & DOWNSPOUTS
A. Material: Aluminum, seamless.
B. Condition: Gutters show multiple small dimples on the west elevation. Downspout on the southwest corner has a visible dent approx. 2" diameter. Gutter seams appear intact. Downspouts are clear and functioning.

1.3 EXTERIOR – SIDING & TRIM
A. Material: Vinyl siding, 4" exposure, color: light gray/tan.
B. Condition: No hail impact observed on siding. Two loose pieces of siding on the east elevation, near the utility meter. The insured stated these were loose before the storm. No trim damage observed.

1.4 EXTERIOR – WINDOWS & DOORS
A. Windows: All vinyl, double-hung. No broken glass. Screens on the west side: 2 screens have small punctures (approx. 1/4"). The insured stated the screens were old and had prior wear.
B. Doors: Front door and storm door appear undamaged. Patio door slider operates normally.

Inspection Report IR-0512 inspection_date 2024-06-10 date. Record status: current.

1.5 DETACHED STRUCTURES
A. Detached Garage (approx. 24' x 24', asphalt shingle roof, 3-tab):
- Hail strikes observed on the south-facing slope. Several shingles have granule loss and bruising. The garage roof is older (est. 12-15 years) and shows general weathering. Impact damage is present but less pronounced than the dwelling.
- No structural issues observed.
B. Shed (approx. 8' x 10', metal roof):
- No hail damage observed. Roof surface has minor surface rust at the seams, consistent with age.

1.6 INTERIOR (for active leaks or water intrusion)
A. Attic: Accessed via pull-down stairs in the hallway. No visible water stains on the roof decking or rafters. No daylight visible through the roof. Insulation (blown fiberglass) appears dry.

SECTION 4: OBSERVED DAMAGE SUMMARY

4.1 ROOF COVERING – DWELLING
- Material: Architectural shingles, Timberline HD, color "Weathered Wood." Estimated age 8 years (per insured, installed 2016).
- Slope orientation: South, west, north, east (hip roof with ridge caps).
- Damage type: Wind and hail damage category. Hail strikes observed on south and west slopes. Strikes are circular, approx. 1/2" to 3/4" diameter, with granule loss and bruising. Some shingles have split sealant tabs. No missing shingles observed.
- Hail size estimate: 1" to 1.25" (quarter to golf ball), based on strike diameter and bruise pattern.
- Wind damage: Ridge cap on west slope has a lifted tab at the rake edge. One shingle on the south slope has a creased corner, consistent with wind uplift. No full shingle loss.
- Granule loss: Moderate to heavy on south slope, moderate on west slope. Granules observed in gutters and on ground below drip edge.
- Age factor: Shingles show normal weathering for 8 years. Damage is distinguishable from wear by the presence of fresh bruising and displaced granules.

4.2 ROOF FLASHING & PENETRATIONS
- Plumbing vent boot (north slope): Rubber collar cracked, approx. 2" tear. Crack is old and brittle, not consistent with impact. Recommend replacement as maintenance item.
- Chimney flashing (north side): Step flashing lifted at one point, approx. 1/4" gap. Likely wind-related. No water intrusion observed at time of inspection.
- Valley flashing: No damage observed. No dents or separation.
- Pipe jack (south slope): No damage. Collar intact.

4.3 GUTTERS & DOWNSPOUTS
- Gutters: Aluminum, seamless. Dimples observed on west elevation gutter, consistent with hail impact. Dimples are approx. 1/4" to 1/2" wide, not perforated.
- Downspouts: One dent on southwest corner downspout, approx. 2" long. No separation or blockage.
- Gutter guards: Not present. Gutters were clean at time of inspection.

4.4 EXTERIOR WALLS & SIDING
- Siding: Vinyl, horizontal lap. East elevation has loose siding panel near the corner, approx. 3' section. Insured stated this was pre-existing (present before the storm). No new damage observed.
- Fascia and soffit: No damage observed. Paint intact.
- Trim: No damage observed.

4.5 DETACHED STRUCTURES (CONTINUED FROM SECTION 1.5)
- Garage: Hail strikes on south slope, granule loss and bruising. Roof is older (est. 12-15 years, 3-tab shingles). Damage present but less pronounced than dwelling. No structural issues.
- Shed: No hail damage. Minor surface rust at seams, consistent with age.

4.6 INTERIOR (CONTINUED FROM SECTION 1.6)
- Attic: No water stains on roof decking or rafters. No daylight visible. Insulation dry.
- Interior rooms: No water stains on ceilings or walls. All rooms checked visually.

Inspection Report IR-0512 reported_roof_damage_type wind and hail damage category. Record status: current.

---

SECTION 5: INSPECTOR'S NOTES & ASSESSMENT

The dwelling roof has sustained wind and hail damage category. The damage is consistent with a hail event and wind uplift, and is distinguishable from normal weathering. The south and west slopes are the most affected. The garage roof has similar but less pronounced damage.

The plumbing vent boot crack and the loose siding on the east elevation are pre-existing conditions and are not related to the reported storm event. The insured acknowledged both items.

No structural concerns were noted. No water intrusion was observed at the time of inspection. The attic was dry.

Recommend full roof replacement for the dwelling. The shingles have moderate to heavy granule loss, and the hail strikes are widespread across two slopes. A repair is not practical due to the extent of damage and the age of the shingles. The garage roof is a candidate for repair or replacement, depending on policy terms and the insured's preference. The shed does not require repair.

Recommend replacement of the plumbing vent boot as a maintenance item, unrelated to the claim.
